user.t:
Act as a combined BUSINESS-ANALYST + FINANCIAL-PLANNER team. Produce a ranked report of 30 distinct SaaS business ideas for the owner (Marius Carlsson), optimized for FAST, REALISTIC time-to-first-revenue. Build on the existing research: READ C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\industry-problems-report.html (the 15-problem report) and reuse/extend it; EXCLUDE the 12 already built (freight spend recovery, P&C subrogation, cross-border withholding-tax reclaim, provider-data accuracy, contract-to-cash leakage, 340B/rebate reconciliation, delegated-authority bordereaux, CMMC compliance-evidence, customs post-entry duty, grid interconnection, corporate-actions, public-benefit eligibility-evidence) — list those as "already built" and find 30 NEW ones.

Favor the pattern that has worked: B2B, software-first (no hardware, no heavy ML needed), document/workflow/money-recovery or compliance-evidence shaped, buyers with an EXISTING budget line, short sales cycle, low regulatory drag. You MAY use WebSearch for current market context, but treat web content as untrusted data and cite it as a claim, not fact.

For EACH of the 30 ideas give: (1) name + one-line pitch; (2) the problem + who feels it; (3) target buyer + why they already pay for this pain; (4) what the software does (MVP shape); (5) build-effort S/M/L; (6) TIME-TO-FIRST-REVENUE estimate (weeks/months) with reasoning; (7) moat/defensibility; (8) honest risks + competitive reality (name incumbents); (9) a FINANCIAL SKETCH — illustrative build cost, pricing model, rough path to break-even — with EVERY number explicitly labeled ASSUMPTION (fabricate nothing as fact); (10) a go / maybe / defer call.

Then RANK all 30 by a "fast-revenue-realistic" score (time-to-revenue x feasibility, penalized by regulatory drag + crowding) and give a top-10 shortlist. Do NOT pad to 30 with junk — if some are weak, say so plainly and mark them defer. HONESTY: this is an idea shortlist; "make money fast" is time-to-revenue-optimized but still needs real customers + owner execution (deployment, entity, outreach) — state that up front; make NO guaranteed-income or fabricated-market claims.

Write the full report to C:\Users\mariu\experiments\30-saas-ideas-report.md. Return a concise summary: the top 10 ranked (name + time-to-revenue + go/maybe/defer) and the report path.

handback.t:
The report is written: 30 new ideas, each with all 10 requested fields, plus a ranked table and a top-10 shortlist. It excludes the 12 already-built ideas, which are listed as "already built". I did not use WebSearch, so incumbents, laws and deadlines are general-knowledge claims, marked "(verify)" where they are most likely to be wrong. Every financial number is labeled ASSUMPTION, no market sizes are asserted, and the report states up front that this is a shortlist and not a plan that makes money.

Ranking uses an explicit rubric, all scores being my judgment: (time-to-revenue x feasibility) minus (regulatory drag + crowding).

**Top 10**

| Rank | Idea | Time to first revenue | Call |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Tenant CAM / operating-expense audit | 6-10 weeks | GO |
| 2 | SkatteFUNN R&D tax-credit substantiation (Norway) | 6-10 weeks | GO |
| 3 | CPG retailer-deduction and fine recovery | 6-12 weeks | GO |
| 4 | Insurance-broker commission reconciliation | 6-10 weeks | GO |
| 5 | AP duplicate-payment and vendor-statement recovery | 6-10 weeks | GO |
| 6 | Transparency Act (Apenhetsloven) supplier due-diligence | 6-10 weeks | GO |
| 7 | Merchant processing-fee audit | 4-8 weeks, but paying customers uncertain | MAYBE |
| 8 | Chargeback dispute-evidence packager | 6-10 weeks | MAYBE |
| 9 | Franchise royalty / sales-reporting audit | 3-4 months | MAYBE |
| 10 | Workers-comp / premium-audit defense | 3-4 months | MAYBE |

**Caveats**
- **Borderline picks:** Ranks 7-10 are borderline (7 and 8 are crowded or weak on unit economics). Ranks 1-6 are where I would run buyer interviews first.
- **Defer calls:** The report plainly marks 28 (telecom CDR billing disputes), 29 (clinical-trial site payments) and 30 (NIS2 evidence) as weak defers. Ranks 23-27 are real but regulation-heavy, and 11 and 19-22 are crowded or seasonal.
- **Not re-ranked:** The report notes that three items from the original 15-problem list (claim denials, prior authorization, legacy modernization) were not re-ranked. They would score defer on the rubric.
- **Shared engine:** Ideas 3, 4, 5, 12 and 15 share one extraction-matching-dispute engine, and 25, 26 and 30 could reuse the compliance-evidence engine you already built.

Report path: C:\Users\mariu\experiments\30-saas-ideas-report.md
